title: TypeScript SDK: Hydrator toolbelt for robust structured output, streaming validation, and retry-safe examples
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Deliver a compact, well-documented 'hydrator' toolbelt in the TypeScript SDK that bridges codegen types, discriminated unions, and runtime validators (Zod/JSON-Schema) with first-class streaming parsing and practical retry examples. This ticket covers API ergonomics, generator flags, streaming partial-validation strategies, and example snippets that demonstrate retry-safe behavior for idempotent vs non-idempotent handlers. The hydrator should emit minimal runtime helpers: (1) union registry with discriminator overrides, (2) lightweight zod adapters that support incremental validation during streaming, (3) json-schema output for integrations, and (4) utility helpers for creating idempotency keys and rehydrating partial-kv cache fragments. Deliverables: codegen changes, runtime helpers, docs, and three end-to-end examples (simple chat, structured invoice extraction, streaming deltas).
acceptance_criteria: Codegen flag --emit-hydrator produces helpers package + types without >5% bundle increase when tree-shaken
Discriminator override is supported via @shape.discriminator('type') in generated types and respected during runtime decoding
Streaming parse API supports incremental zod checks: header-level schema validated first, body fields validated as they arrive
Retry example demonstrates safe replays for idempotent updates and a recommended pattern for non-idempotent operations (use server-side dedup + client idempotency keys)
Unit tests for union registry, streaming validator, and idempotency helper reach >= 90% coverage for new modules
Docs and three runnable examples added to examples/ts-sdk/hydrator with README and GitHub Actions workflow that runs them against a local dev model runtime
